Subject: piano accordion.

reasoning:
I'm picturing a piano accordion with two boxes—treble side with piano keys, bass side with buttons—connected by bellows, finished in a pearly iridescent white/pink/teal with gilt trim and red bellows, standing upright with the bellows axis running horizontally.

Working out the exact dimensions and positioning: treble box on one side, bass box on the other, bellows spanning between them, with keys facing one direction and bass buttons facing the back where the strap would attach.

Now I'm planning the full component list: pearl-painted treble box with gilt trim and an ornamental grille texture on the end plate, a bass box with cylindrical pearl buttons in a grid and a strap loop, and the bellows built as a stack of alternating frustum folds.

I'll add thin gilt corner rods on the bellows corners, then skip the complex drooping shoulder strap and simplify to a bass hand strap with buckle plus small top anchor loops instead.

Register switches go on the treble top as rows of small pearl pieces with gilt accents, plus a master switch; I'll keep joints minimal with a static root body rather than rigging the bellows. For paint, I'm using noise-based pearl iridescence mixing white, pink, and teal with mottling, red grained bellows paint, and gilt metal shading, with both boxes resting flush on the floor.

I'm also planning decorative details: a grille pattern with perforations, a gilt "ROSSINI" brand plate on black for the treble front, and mother-of-pearl floral inlay patterns on the bass side and treble front using simple SVG shapes. Writing box helper code...

For the pearl material, I'm defining a paint function that blends warm ivory and pink-grey tones through layered noise and smoothstep transitions, with a sheen based on surface normal. I'm also laying out the treble and bass box dimensions and positions, figuring out where the keyboard plate and keys sit on the front face.

Now I'm working out the keyboard geometry: white keys spanning along y with set spacing, black keys interspersed following a pattern that skips certain positions, offset outward in x and raised slightly higher in z than the white keys. I'm starting to define the bellows dimensions next.

Adding ridge thickness variation, then placing gilt corner guard rods connecting bass-to-treble bellows corners, and sketching small pearl register boxes on top.

Still placing switch rows and gilt trim frames at top/bottom rims, then laying out the bass-side button grid along the -Z face.

Now I'm adding the gilt-bordered black plate behind the buttons, making each pearl cylinder button face down along z with every third one marked gold as a "C" reference. I'm also placing the bass end's fabric inlay plane and the treble end's grille plane, sizing them to fit the accordion body symmetrically.

For simplicity I'll place both the treble keys and bass buttons facing the same +Z direction, along with rosette inlays, brand plate, and leather hand straps on the back faces, rather than worrying about strict left/right player orientation.

Now I'm adding shoulder strap loops as arcing catmull-rom ribbon sweeps connecting the top of the treble back to the top of the bass back, giving a floating folded-strap look across the accordion's upper edge.

For decoration, I'm planning pearl-inlay rosette textures with teal and pink petal patterns on the bass end plate and treble brand plate, plus cheek plates for the bellows.

Writing part definitions...
